title: Import Project: review real masks, measurements and provenance
description: Import an actual two-field microscopy subset, review object joins and column names before writing, and distinguish imported measurements from a fresh spaCR measurement run.
objectives: Find Import Project and its three nested input tools.
Pair images, instance masks and a measurement table, with explicit units and object identities.
Review inferred names, demonstrate and resolve a reserved-name conflict, and save and reload the mapping.
Verify imported pixels, per-object values and provenance without claiming that import remeasures the data.
prerequisite: Download Measure's example first. prepare_inputs in tools/tutorials/capture_foreign.py extracts unchanged ER intensity plane 1 and cell-label plane 4 from plate1_E01_1_1 and plate1_L02_9_1. It recomputes exact pixel areas and raw mean intensities from those same labels, producing 103 real measurement rows. Neutral fov01/fov02 TIFF names deliberately require the saved source manifest to recover original acquisition wells; they do not preserve plate layout automatically. No physical pixel calibration is asserted.

scenes.narration: Open Import in Home's Data category. This parent workflow adopts existing images, instance masks and measurements. It is different from starting with raw microscope files and generating new masks and measurements in spaCR.

The header now hosts Import Images, Format Converter and External Masks. Use Import Images for raw acquisitions, Format Converter for supported format conversion, and External Masks for existing segmentation labels. Their specialist lessons remain under Import in the Submodules section.

This recording reuses two real fields from Measure's downloaded example. Separate TIFF copies preserve the original intensity and label pixels. Our preparation recipe measures pixel area and mean intensity from those exact labels, instead of mixing masks with an independently versioned measurement table.

Choose the image folder, then the Cell mask folder and press Add. These are instance labels, not a binary foreground image. Our example contains one intensity channel and one mask class. Add other classes only when they genuinely describe the corresponding fields.

Choose the actual measurement CSV. ImageNumber identifies each prepared image, and ObjectNumber identifies its label inside that field. A label number alone is not unique across images. The table contains one hundred and three measured objects, not synthetic rows added to make a join pass.

Leave micrometres per pixel blank when calibration is unknown. Our area column explicitly uses pixels squared, and intensity is a raw image mean. Do not enter an invented scale. Physical-unit columns require separate review; an uncalibrated value must not be described as a converted pixel measurement.

Preview writes no project data. The current importer conservatively proposes foreign-prefixed column names, including foreign_cell_area for a source already called cell_area. Its note is not a blocking error: inference has avoided overwriting a spaCR feature, but the scientific meaning still needs your review.

Select a target cell and press F two to edit it. Here we deliberately change the area target to the reserved name cell_area. With Refuse the import selected, this actual conflicting edit disables Import. Nothing has been written; do not treat the demonstration target as a recommended mapping.

Choosing the Rename policy resolves the conflict without overwriting spaCR's feature. Read the join report: all one hundred and three table rows match real mask objects, with no unmeasured objects in this subset. Row counts alone would not detect values assigned to the wrong field or label.

Give the area an explicit reviewed target, foreign_reviewed_area_px2. The mapping updates in place. Review the source, target, transform and units together: renaming a column does not establish that two laboratories measured the same biological quantity.

Save mapping writes the reviewed column definitions to a CSV. It is not a backup of your images or a complete acquisition manifest. Keep the source files and their identity records as well as the mapping, so the decisions can be audited later.

Load mapping reads those definitions back into the current plan. We first make a temporary unsaved target change; selecting the saved CSV then restores the reviewed name. Check the plan again when source files, labels or units differ. A reusable mapping is not automatic approval of a new experiment.

Press Import for the reviewed plan and inspect the actual report. This run converts two image files, writes two masks and two merged arrays, and stores one hundred and three rows in each of two object tables. The status total of two hundred and six counts both tables, not twice as many distinct objects.

The summary explicitly says spaCR did not re-extract measurements. The foreign_columns table records which values came from this import. Our checks confirm original pixels, labels, and each object's area and mean intensity survive the conversion; that is different from validating the biological interpretation.

Our neutral fov names become new fields in A zero one; they do not reconstruct the original acquisition wells. Retain the preparation manifest and conversion map. For a real plate experiment, resolve acquisition identities before downstream analysis instead of treating newly assigned coordinates as original metadata.

In Python, spacr.foreign provides plan_import, save_column_map, load_column_map and run_import for the same review-and-apply boundary. Keep the reviewed mapping with the completed project. Use Measure when you actually want spaCR to compute new features, rather than assuming an import already did so.
